set.body:
Scope

Add a runtime factor-level schema suitable for BIDS-loaded data, with optional ergonomic derivation for Scala enums. Do not require compile-time table schemas.

Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Factor level identity and ordering are declared independently of first-observed row order.
- [ ] Scala enums may derive a stable level set; externally coded string/numeric factors provide an explicit validated level registry.
- [ ] Construction rejects duplicate identities, unknown observed levels, inconsistent coding, and incompatible cross-run level schemas with typed errors.
- [ ] Empty-cell policy is explicit: reject, retain a structurally present zero column, or omit with an audit receipt.
- [ ] CellKey uses declared FactorId/LevelId assignments and remains stable across event-row permutations and subjects with absent cells.
- [ ] DesignAudit records declared, observed, empty, retained, and omitted cells and the selected policy.
- [ ] Contrast compilation distinguishes unknown levels from declared-but-empty/non-estimable levels.
- [ ] Existing Event.factor remains a documented convenience adapter and cannot silently become the authority for multi-run/subject alignment.
- [ ] JVM and Scala.js tests cover reordered observations, absent cells, unknown levels, mixed runs, and compatibility rendering.
set.title: P2.1: declare stable factor levels and explicit empty-cell policy
